name.detail: Driving while under the influence of an alcoholic beverage, inhalant, or controlled substance.

bacLimit.detail: It is a crime to drive with a blood or breath alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more within four hours of driving.

under21.detail: Drivers aged 14 to 20 commit an offense by driving after consuming any quantity of alcohol.

commercial.detail: Commercial vehicle drivers are guilty of DUI with a blood or breath alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings an administrative revocation of at least 90 days; refusal is also a separate crime with penalties matching DUI.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first DUI conviction requires an ignition interlock for at least 6 months after driving privileges return (waivable in certain remote communities).

lookback.detail: A person is 'previously convicted' if convicted of DUI or refusal within the 15 years before the current offense.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol, controlled substances, or other impairing substances.

bacLimit.detail: It is a crime to drive with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive with 0.02 percent or more alcohol in their blood.

commercial.detail: Commercial motor vehicle drivers may not drive with 0.04 percent or more alcohol in their blood.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal (no prior alcohol/drug contacts in 10 years) brings a 90-day administrative suspension; a conviction also carries a 1-year interlock requirement.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Required at high BAC (0.15%+) or aggravating factors
interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first offender must use an interlock for 1 year if BAC was 0.15%+, they refused testing, a child under 14 was aboard, or someone was injured; others may choose one to stay the 90-day suspension.

lookback.detail: Prior DUI convictions within 10 years count for sentencing; after a felony DUI, all later DUIs are felonies regardless of date.

name.detail: Driving while intoxicated (DUI is the separate underage offense).

bacLimit.detail: A driver with a blood alcohol level of 0.08% or more is considered intoxicated.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with a BAC of at least 0.02% but under 0.08% commit Underage DUI.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 180-day suspension; a second within 5 years brings 2 years.

lookback.detail: Since Act 274 of 2021, prior DWIs within 10 years count for repeat-offense jail terms; license-suspension tiers still use 5 years.
lookback.cite: Ark. Code Ann. § 5-65-111 (as amended by Act 274 of 2021)

name.detail: Driving under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs.

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more within two hours of driving.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive with any spirituous liquor in their body (zero tolerance).

commercial.detail: Commercial motor vehicle drivers (and for-hire/rideshare drivers) are guilty of DUI at 0.04 or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 12-month administrative suspension (2 years for a second within 84 months), separate from any criminal case.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: After a first DUI conviction involving alcohol, the MVD requires a certified ignition interlock on any vehicle the person drives.

lookback.detail: A DUI within 84 months of a prior DUI conviction is sentenced as a repeat offense.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol and/or drugs.

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive with a BAC of 0.01% or more (license suspension); 0.05% or more is an infraction under § 23140.

commercial.detail: It is unlawful to drive a commercial motor vehicle with a BAC of 0.04 percent or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 1-year suspension (2-3 year revocation with priors in 10 years), in addition to enhanced criminal penalties if convicted.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: For a first DUI without injury, a court may order an interlock or the driver may choose an interlock-restricted license; a first DUI causing injury requires one.

lookback.detail: A DUI within 10 years of a prior DUI or wet reckless conviction is punished as a repeat offense.

name.detail: Driving under the influence; Colorado also has DUI per se and the lesser DWAI (driving while ability impaired).

bacLimit.detail: Driving with a BAC of 0.08 or more at the time of driving or within two hours after is DUI per se.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with a BAC of 0.02 to 0.05 commit a traffic infraction and face license revocation (UDD).

commercial.detail: The license of a commercial driver with a BAC of 0.04 or more ('excess BAC CDL') is revoked under federal disqualification periods.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 1-year administrative revocation (2 years for a second, 3 for a third).

lookback.detail: Colorado counts prior DUI/DWAI convictions regardless of age; a DUI with three or more priors at any time is a felony.

name.detail: Operating under the influence of liquor or drugs or with an elevated blood alcohol content (often called OUI or DUI).

bacLimit.detail: 'Elevated blood alcohol content' for drivers 21 and older means 0.08 percent or more by weight.

under21.detail: For drivers under 21, an elevated blood alcohol content is 0.02 percent or more, triggering license suspension.

commercial.detail: For commercial motor vehicle drivers, an elevated blood alcohol content is 0.04 percent or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 45-day administrative suspension, then a 1-year ignition interlock requirement to drive.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first conviction brings a 45-day suspension, then 1 year of driving only vehicles equipped with an ignition interlock.

lookback.detail: Second and third offense penalties apply when the new violation is within 10 years of a prior conviction.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol or a drug; D.C. also has the lesser offense of operating while impaired (OWI).

bacLimit.detail: 'Intoxicated' includes having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 grams or more per 100 mL of blood or 210 L of breath.

under21.detail: For drivers under 21, any measurable amount of alcohol in blood, breath, or urine means they are legally intoxicated.

commercial.detail: For commercial vehicle drivers, an alcohol concentration of 0.04 grams or more means they are legally intoxicated.

refusalSuspension.detail: A refusal brings a 12-month revocation of the privilege to drive in D.C.; D.C. license holders may instead be required to enroll in the interlock program.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: D.C. license holders who commit a first DUI or OWI must enroll in the Ignition Interlock System Program for 6 months.

lookback.detail: A prior offense counts unless the sentence (incarceration, probation, parole) ended more than 15 years before the current arrest.

name.detail: Driving a vehicle while under the influence or with a prohibited alcohol or drug content.

bacLimit.detail: It is a crime to drive with an alcohol concentration of .08 or more, including within 4 hours after driving.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive after consuming alcohol; a BAC of .02 or more is per se evidence of the violation.

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of .04 or more is a crime and leads to CDL disqualification.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal (no DUI or refusal in prior 5 years) brings a 1-year administrative revocation.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Required only to drive during revocation
interlockFirstOffense.detail: First offenders face a 12-24 month revocation and may drive during it only with an interlock license; IIHS does not list it as a mandatory penalty.

lookback.detail: A second DUI within 10 years is a repeat offense; a third or later DUI is a felony no matter when the priors occurred.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol, chemical substances, or controlled substances.

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with a blood or breath alcohol level of 0.08 or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with a blood or breath alcohol level of 0.02 or higher face a 6-month administrative license suspension.

commercial.detail: Commercial vehicle drivers with a blood or breath alcohol level of 0.04 or more are subject to disqualification penalties.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 1-year administrative suspension (18 months if previously suspended for refusal); a second refusal is also a misdemeanor.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: An interlock for at least 6 months is mandatory on a first conviction with BAC of 0.15%+ or a minor in the vehicle; otherwise it is discretionary.

lookback.detail: A second DUI within 5 years brings mandatory jail; a third within 10 years is a felony; a fourth DUI at any time is a felony.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or other intoxicating substances.

refusalSuspension.detail: Refusing state-administered chemical testing brings a license suspension of at least 1 year.

name.detail: Operating a vehicle under the influence of an intoxicant.

bacLimit.detail: It is an offense to drive with .08 or more grams of alcohol per 210 liters of breath or 100 mL of blood.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive with a 'measurable amount' of alcohol, defined as a BAC of .02 up to .08.

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more is a disqualifying offense and prohibited.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal (no prior contacts in 10 years) brings a 2-year administrative revocation, with an ignition interlock required to drive during it.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first conviction brings a 1-to-18-month revocation with an ignition interlock installed on all vehicles operated during the revocation.

lookback.detail: An OVUII within 10 years of a prior conviction is punished as a repeat offense; three in 10 years can be habitual (felony) OVUII.

name.detail: Operating while intoxicated.

bacLimit.detail: It is an offense to operate a motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of .08 or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with an alcohol concentration of .02 or more (but under .08) face license revocation.

commercial.detail: Operating a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more brings a 1-year CDL disqualification.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 1-year administrative revocation (2 years with a prior revocation); a restricted license requires an interlock.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Required only for a restricted license
interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first offender who wants a temporary restricted license during the 180-day-to-1-year revocation must install an ignition interlock.

lookback.detail: Prior OWI convictions count until they are deleted from the driving record 12 years after conviction.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or other intoxicating substances.

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive with an alcohol concentration of at least 0.02 but less than 0.08.

commercial.detail: It is unlawful to drive a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a $250 civil penalty, a 1-year absolute suspension, and 1 year of interlock after the suspension ends.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: After a 30-day absolute suspension, a first offender must install an interlock within 10 days and keep it until 1 year after the suspension ends, unless excused.

lookback.detail: A second DUI within 10 years is a repeat offense; a DUI with two or more priors within 10 years is a felony.

name.detail: Driving while under the influence of alcohol, other drugs, or intoxicating compounds.

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with any alcohol (a concentration above 0.00) face license suspension under the zero-tolerance law.

commercial.detail: Operating a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more brings at least a 12-month CDL disqualification.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first offender who refuses testing gets a 12-month statutory summary suspension (3 years for non-first offenders).

interlockFirstOffense.value: Optional (required only to drive during suspension)
interlockFirstOffense.detail: First offenders may drive during the summary suspension only with a Monitoring Device Driving Permit and an interlock; interlock is mandatory for 5 years after a second conviction.

lookback.detail: Illinois counts prior DUIs regardless of age; a third DUI at any time is a Class 2 felony.

name.detail: Operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

bacLimit.detail: Driving with a blood alcohol concentration above the .08 legal limit is a criminal offense.

refusalSuspension.detail: Refusing a chemical test brings a 1-year suspension (2 years with a prior OWI conviction).

interlockFirstOffense.detail: Indiana does not require interlocks for first offenders; a court may order one, for example as a condition of specialized driving privileges.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, including as measured within three hours of driving.

under21.detail: It is unlawful for anyone under 21 to drive with a breath or blood alcohol content of .02 or greater.

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more is commercial DUI.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 1-year suspension followed by 2 years of interlock-only driving; refusal can also be prosecuted separately.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: After a 30-day suspension, a first offender is restricted to interlock-equipped vehicles for 180 days (1 year if BAC was 0.15%+).

lookback.detail: All DUI convictions or diversions occurring on or after July 1, 2001 count when deciding whether an offense is a repeat.

name.detail: Operating a motor vehicle under the influence of alcohol or other impairing substances.

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to operate a vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not operate a vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or more.

commercial.detail: A commercial driver with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more is deemed to be driving under the influence and is disqualified.

refusalSuspension.value: Suspended pending case; 6 months if found to have refused
refusalSuspension.detail: Kentucky has no fixed administrative refusal term: the court suspends the license at arraignment, and if the driver is not convicted but refused, for the first-offense period.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first offender may drive during the suspension only with an ignition interlock license; there is no mandatory interlock penalty for all first offenders.

lookback.detail: Repeat-offense penalties apply to DUI offenses within a 10-year period; a fourth within 10 years is a felony.

name.detail: Operating a vehicle while impaired; commonly called DWI.

bacLimit.detail: It is a crime to operate a vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 commit underage operating while impaired with a BAC of 0.02 percent or more.

commercial.detail: Commercial drivers with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 percent or more face CDL disqualification.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 1-year administrative suspension (2 years with a prior refusal).

interlockFirstOffense.value: Required for all first offenses (if on probation)
interlockFirstOffense.detail: As a probation condition, a first offender may drive for at least 6 months only in an interlock-equipped vehicle; 0.20%+ BAC also requires one during suspension.

lookback.detail: Prior impaired-driving convictions older than 10 years do not count, excluding time spent incarcerated, on probation or parole, or awaiting trial.

name.detail: Operating under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs.

bacLimit.detail: It is a crime to operate a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol percentage of eight one-hundredths (0.08) or greater.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with a BAC of 0.02 or greater have their license suspended for 180 days (longer if under 18).

commercial.detail: Operating a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more is a disqualifying offense.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal by a driver 21+ with no prior OUI brings a 180-day suspension; under-21 drivers and repeat offenders face longer terms.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Not required (only for some hardship licenses)
interlockFirstOffense.detail: Massachusetts does not require interlocks for first offenders; the registrar may require one on a hardship license if BAC was 0.15%+.

lookback.detail: Any prior OUI conviction or alcohol-program assignment, no matter how old, counts toward repeat-offense penalties.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol (DUI) and the lesser offense of driving while impaired by alcohol (DWI).

bacLimit.detail: Driving 'under the influence of alcohol per se' means having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more.

under21.detail: Licenses of drivers under 21 carry an alcohol restriction barring driving with any alcohol in the blood.

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more is a disqualifying offense.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first test refusal brings a 270-day administrative suspension (2 years for a second); the driver may instead join the Ignition Interlock Program.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Required for all DUI first offenses
interlockFirstOffense.detail: Anyone convicted of DUI or DUI per se (or given probation before judgment) must complete the Ignition Interlock Program, 6 months for a first time.

name.detail: Operating under the influence of intoxicants.

bacLimit.detail: It is a crime to operate a motor vehicle with an alcohol level of 0.08 grams or more per 100 mL of blood or 210 L of breath.

under21.detail: Licenses of drivers under 21 carry the condition that they not drive with an alcohol level above 0.00; violation brings suspension.

commercial.detail: A commercial vehicle operator with an alcohol level of 0.04 or more faces testing and disqualification under the commercial implied-consent law.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 275-day suspension (18 months for a second); refusal also increases criminal penalties if convicted.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: Maine does not mandate an interlock for first offenders; installing one can shorten the mandatory suspension period.

lookback.detail: Repeat OUI penalties apply based on previous OUI offenses within a 10-year period.

name.detail: Operating while intoxicated (also the lesser offense of operating while visibly impaired).

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to operate a vehicle with an alcohol content of 0.08 grams or more; 0.17 or more is 'high BAC' OWI with tougher penalties.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not operate with an alcohol content of 0.02 or more (but under 0.08) or with any bodily alcohol content.

commercial.detail: Operating a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol content of 0.04 or more (but under 0.08) is a separate misdemeanor.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 1-year license suspension (2 years for a refusal within 7 years of a prior), plus 6 points.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Required at high BAC (0.17%+) to drive
interlockFirstOffense.detail: First offenders convicted of high-BAC OWI (0.17%+) may drive on a restricted license only with an interlock; otherwise a court may order one as a probation condition.

lookback.detail: A second OWI within 7 years is a repeat offense; a third OWI is a felony regardless of how long ago the priors occurred.

name.detail: Driving while impaired.

bacLimit.detail: It is a crime to drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more at the time of driving or within two hours.

under21.detail: It is a crime for anyone under 21 to drive after consuming alcohol while physical evidence of consumption is present in their body.

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more is DWI.

refusalSuspension.detail: With no qualified prior incident in 20 years, a refusal brings at least a 1-year revocation; test refusal is also a separate crime.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: Interlock is mandatory for repeat offenders; first offenders may choose the interlock program to regain driving privileges during revocation.

lookback.detail: Prior impaired-driving incidents within 10 years enhance criminal charges; four in 10 years is a felony. License revocation tiers look back 20 years.

name.detail: Driving while intoxicated; Missouri also has driving with excessive blood alcohol content (BAC).

bacLimit.detail: Driving with eight-hundredths of one percent or more alcohol by weight is the offense of excessive blood alcohol content.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 stopped with a BAC of 0.02% or more face administrative license suspension.

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04% or more is a disqualifying offense.

refusalSuspension.detail: Refusing a chemical test brings an immediate 1-year license revocation, separate from any criminal DWI case.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first offender whose BAC was 0.15% or more (or who caused damage or injury) must use an interlock for at least 6 months after reinstatement.

lookback.detail: A 'prior offender' has one intoxication-related offense within 5 years; persistent, aggravated, and chronic offender tiers count priors regardless of age.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of intoxicating liquor or other impairing substances.

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with a blood alcohol concentration of .08% or more (for drivers 21 and older).

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive with a blood alcohol concentration of .02% or more.

commercial.detail: Commercial vehicle drivers may not drive with a blood alcohol concentration of .04% or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal (no prior DUI conviction or nonadjudication) brings a 90-day administrative suspension, in addition to DUI penalties; 1 year with a prior.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first offense brings a 120-day suspension; the driver may instead drive on an interlock-restricted license, so an interlock is not mandatory.

lookback.detail: Second and third DUI offense penalties apply when the offenses were committed within a 5-year period.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs (Montana also has a separate per se offense).

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive a noncommercial vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or more.

commercial.detail: It is unlawful to drive a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 6-month suspension with no restricted license (1 year for a repeat within 5 years).

interlockFirstOffense.detail: For a first DUI, the court may require an ignition interlock (or 24/7 sobriety monitoring) as a condition of a probationary license.

lookback.detail: Prior DUIs count if within 10 years, but for a third or later offense all previous convictions are counted.

name.detail: Impaired driving, commonly called DWI.

bacLimit.detail: It is a crime to drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more at any relevant time after driving.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive while consuming alcohol or with any alcohol remaining in their body.

commercial.detail: It is a crime to drive a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A willful refusal brings a 12-month license revocation by the DMV, in addition to the immediate 30-day civil revocation.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first offender whose alcohol concentration was 0.15 or more must use an ignition interlock for 1 year after license restoration.

lookback.detail: A prior DWI within 7 years is a grossly aggravating sentencing factor; three or more priors within 10 years make a new DWI a felony (habitual DWI).

name.detail: Driving under the influence of intoxicating liquor, drugs, or other substances (also actual physical control, APC).

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with an alcohol concentration of at least 0.08 percent within two hours of driving.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with an alcohol concentration of at least 0.02 percent face administrative license suspension.

commercial.detail: Commercial drivers with an alcohol concentration of at least 0.04 percent face CDL disqualification.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal (no prior suspension in 7 years) brings a 180-day revocation; 2 years with one prior.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: North Dakota does not require ignition interlocks for DUI offenders; it relies on the 24/7 sobriety program instead.

lookback.detail: Repeat penalties apply to offenses within 7 years; a fourth or later offense within 15 years is a felony.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcoholic liquor or drugs.

bacLimit.detail: It is a crime to drive with .08 grams or more of alcohol per 100 mL of blood or 210 L of breath.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive with an alcohol concentration of .02 or more (but below .08).

commercial.detail: Commercial drivers found with .04 or more alcohol face CDL disqualification under the commercial implied-consent law.

refusalSuspension.detail: A refusal brings a 1-year administrative license revocation; the driver may apply for an ignition interlock permit. Refusal is also a crime.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Required for all first offenses (to drive during revocation)
interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first conviction brings a 6-month revocation (1 year at .15+), and the order requires an ignition interlock permit and device to drive during it.

lookback.detail: A 'prior conviction' for sentencing is one for a violation committed within the 15 years before the current offense.

name.detail: Driving while intoxicated (aggravated DWI is a separate, more serious offense).

bacLimit.detail: It is an offense to drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 commit DWI with an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or more.

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more is a CDL-disqualifying offense.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal currently brings a 180-day administrative suspension (2 years with a prior); this rises to 9 months on January 1, 2027.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: For a first DWI the court may order an interlock; it is mandatory for aggravated DWI, which includes driving with a BAC of 0.16 or more.

lookback.detail: Second and subsequent offense penalties apply to prior convictions within 10 years of the new offense.

name.detail: Driving while intoxicated (the NJ MVC also uses 'DUI').

bacLimit.detail: It is an offense to operate a motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08% or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with a BAC of 0.01% or more (but under 0.08%) face a 30-90 day suspension, community service, and education.

commercial.detail: Commercial drivers face disqualification with an alcohol concentration of .04% or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal is a court-imposed penalty: driving privileges are forfeited until an interlock is installed, then kept 9-15 months. NJ has no administrative suspension.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: Every first offender must install an interlock: 3 months at 0.08-0.10% BAC, longer at 0.10%+, plus forfeiture periods at higher BACs.

lookback.detail: A second offense more than 10 years after the first is sentenced as a first offense; a third more than 10 years after the second is sentenced as a second.

name.detail: Driving while intoxicated or under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs.

bacLimit.detail: Drivers 21 and older are subject to revocation and prosecution at an alcohol concentration of .08 or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 face license revocation at an alcohol concentration of .02 or more.

commercial.detail: Commercial driver's license holders face revocation at an alcohol concentration of .04 or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal of a chemical test brings a 1-year administrative revocation under the Implied Consent Act.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: Everyone convicted of DWI, including first-time offenders, must get an ignition interlock license and install an interlock device.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of intoxicating liquor or a controlled substance.

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with a concentration of alcohol of 0.08 or more, including when measured within 2 hours of driving.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or more (but under 0.08) have their license suspended for 90 days.

commercial.detail: It is unlawful to drive a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: Failing to submit to an evidentiary test brings a 1-year revocation (3 years with a prior refusal in 7 years); an interlock privilege may be available.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: A court must order an ignition interlock for 185 days after a first DUI conviction within 7 years, with narrow medical/distance exceptions.

lookback.detail: DUI offenses are counted as first, second, or third offenses based on convictions within 7 years; a third within 7 years is a felony.

name.detail: Driving while intoxicated (DWAI, driving while ability impaired, is a lesser offense).

bacLimit.detail: No person may drive with .08 of one percent or more by weight of alcohol in the blood (per se DWI).

under21.detail: Under the Zero Tolerance law, drivers under 21 with a BAC of .02 to .07 face administrative license suspension.

commercial.detail: No one may drive a commercial motor vehicle with a BAC of .04 or more; .04-.06 is a separate per se offense.

refusalSuspension.detail: A refusal brings an administrative license revocation of at least 1 year (18 months with a prior within 5 years) plus a civil penalty.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: Under Leandra's Law, courts must order an ignition interlock for at least 12 months as a condition of probation or conditional discharge for any DWI.

lookback.detail: A DWI within 10 years of a prior DWI conviction is a felony; DWAI repeat penalties also use 10 years.

name.detail: Operating a vehicle under the influence of alcohol and/or drugs.

bacLimit.detail: It is illegal to drive with a blood or breath alcohol concentration of .08 or more; .17 or more is a 'high test' with tougher penalties.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive with a concentration of at least .02 but less than .08.

commercial.detail: No one may drive a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of .04 or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal (no priors in 10 years) brings an administrative license suspension of Class C, which is 1 year.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Required at high BAC (0.17%+) for limited privileges
interlockFirstOffense.detail: First offenders with a 'high test' (.17+) who receive limited driving privileges must use an interlock; otherwise interlock is optional and earns unlimited privileges.

lookback.detail: OVI repeat-offense penalties apply to prior convictions within 10 years of the new offense.

name.detail: Driving while under the influence of intoxicants.

bacLimit.detail: It is DUII to drive with 0.08 percent or more alcohol by weight in the blood, including within two hours after driving.

under21.detail: For drivers under 21, any amount of alcohol in the blood counts as being under the influence for implied-consent license suspension.

commercial.detail: Commercial drivers with 0.04 percent or more alcohol face a 1-year suspension of commercial driving privileges.

refusalSuspension.detail: Refusing a breath or blood test brings a 1-year suspension (3 years with recent priors or diversion); refusal can also bring a fine.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: After a first DUII conviction, ODOT requires an interlock for 1 year after the suspension ends (and as a condition of any hardship permit).

lookback.detail: DUII becomes a Class C felony if the person has three or more DUII convictions in the 10 years before the current offense.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance.

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with a BAC of 0.08% or more within two hours after driving (0.08-0.10% is 'general impairment').

under21.detail: Minors (under 21) may not drive with a BAC of 0.02% or higher within two hours after driving.

commercial.detail: Commercial vehicle drivers may not drive with a BAC of 0.04% or more (0.02% for school buses and school vehicles).

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 12-month suspension (18 months with prior refusal or DUI), plus enhanced criminal penalties if convicted.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Required if license suspended (BAC 0.10%+ or refusal)
interlockFirstOffense.detail: An interlock is a condition of license restoration whenever a DUI or refusal led to suspension; first offenders at 0.08-0.10% have no suspension and no interlock.

lookback.detail: Prior DUI convictions, ARD acceptances, or similar dispositions count if within 10 years before the date of the current offense.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of liquor or drugs.

bacLimit.detail: It is an offense to drive with a blood alcohol concentration of .08% or more.

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with a BAC of .04% or more is DUI and a CDL-disqualifying offense.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal is a civil violation in the Traffic Tribunal with a $200-$500 fine, community service, and a 6-month to 1-year suspension.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: For a first DUI, the judge may require an ignition interlock and/or blood and urine testing as a condition of driving.

lookback.detail: Second and subsequent offense penalties apply to violations within a 10-year period.

name.detail: Driving under the influence; South Carolina also has the per se offense of driving with an unlawful alcohol concentration (DUAC).

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with an alcohol concentration of eight one-hundredths of one percent or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or more have their license suspended.

commercial.detail: A commercial driver with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more must be disqualified from driving a commercial vehicle.

refusalSuspension.detail: With no prior DUI or suspension in 10 years, a refusal brings a 6-month administrative suspension (or an interlock-restricted license).

interlockFirstOffense.detail: The DMV must require an ignition interlock for anyone convicted of DUI or DUAC (unless a .00 breath test), including first offenders.

lookback.detail: Only DUI violations within the 10 years preceding the latest violation count as prior offenses.

name.detail: Driving or being in actual physical control of a vehicle while under the influence or with a prohibited blood alcohol level.

bacLimit.detail: No person may drive with 0.08 percent or more alcohol by weight in the blood.

under21.detail: It is a misdemeanor for anyone under 21 to drive with 0.02 percent or more alcohol in the blood.

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with 0.04 percent or more alcohol brings at least a 1-year CDL disqualification.

refusalSuspension.detail: If a refusal is upheld, the Secretary of Public Safety revokes the license for 1 year (a work permit may be available).

interlockFirstOffense.detail: South Dakota has no mandatory interlock for first offenders; it relies on the 24/7 sobriety program and court-ordered restrictions.

lookback.detail: A prior DUI more than 10 years before the current violation cannot be used to make it a second, third, or subsequent offense.

name.detail: Driving while intoxicated.

bacLimit.detail: 'Intoxicated' includes having an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more.

under21.detail: A minor (under 21) commits an offense by driving with any detectable amount of alcohol in their system.

commercial.detail: A commercial driver with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more while operating a commercial vehicle is disqualified.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal (no prior alcohol contacts in 10 years) brings a 180-day administrative license suspension.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: On community supervision for a first DWI, the court must order an interlock if BAC was 0.15 or more; otherwise it is discretionary (also required for an occupational license).

lookback.detail: Texas enhancement statutes count prior DWI convictions without any time limit; a third DWI is a felony.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or a combination, or with a prohibited alcohol concentration.

bacLimit.detail: Utah has the nation's lowest limit: it is DUI to drive with a blood or breath alcohol concentration of .05 grams or greater.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive with any measurable blood, breath, or urine alcohol concentration ('not a drop').

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of .04 grams or more is a CDL-disqualifying offense.

refusalSuspension.detail: Drivers 21+ who refuse a chemical test lose their license for 18 months (36 months with a prior in 10 years); under 21, until age 21 or 2 years.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Required (court may waive on the record)
interlockFirstOffense.detail: A court must require an interlock for anyone convicted of DUI and placed on probation unless it states on the record the device is unnecessary; mandatory if under 21.

lookback.detail: A DUI is a repeat offense if there is a prior conviction within 10 years; two or more priors within 10 years make it a third-degree felony.

name.detail: Driving while intoxicated; Virginia statutes and courts use DUI and DWI interchangeably.

bacLimit.detail: It is unlawful to drive with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 percent or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with a BAC of 0.02% or more (but under 0.08%) lose their license for 1 year and face a fine or community service.

commercial.detail: It is unlawful to drive a commercial motor vehicle with a BAC of 0.04 percent or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal is a civil offense: the court suspends the license for 1 year, on top of a 7-day administrative suspension at arrest.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first offender who receives a restricted license must use an interlock for at least 12 consecutive months without violations; it is not otherwise mandatory.

lookback.detail: Repeat-offense penalties apply to priors within 10 years (stiffer within 5); a third DUI within 10 years is a felony.

name.detail: Operating a vehicle under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs.

bacLimit.detail: No one may operate a vehicle on a highway with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.02 or more; since July 1, 2025 this is a civil violation under Title 7.

commercial.detail: No one may operate a commercial vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal brings a 6-month civil suspension; an ignition interlock restricted license may be available during it.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: First offenders are not required to use an interlock but may drive during the suspension with an ignition interlock restricted driver's license.

lookback.detail: A second offense is a DUI within 20 years of a prior conviction; a third requires two priors, at least one within 20 years.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of intoxicating liquor, cannabis, or any drug.

bacLimit.detail: It is DUI to have an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or higher within two hours after driving.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with an alcohol concentration of at least 0.02 (but below 0.08) within two hours commit a misdemeanor.

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more is a CDL-disqualifying offense.

refusalSuspension.detail: A first refusal within 7 years brings a 1-year administrative revocation (2 years with a prior incident).

interlockFirstOffense.detail: After any DUI conviction, the Department of Licensing restricts the person to interlock-equipped vehicles once the mandatory suspension ends.

lookback.detail: Mandatory DUI penalties use priors within 7 years; DUI is a felony with three or more priors within 15 years.

name.detail: Operating while intoxicated (also operating with a prohibited alcohol concentration, PAC).

bacLimit.detail: The prohibited alcohol concentration is 0.08 for drivers with two or fewer priors (more than 0.02 with three or more priors or an interlock order).

under21.detail: Drivers under the legal drinking age (21) may not drive with an alcohol concentration of more than 0.0.

commercial.detail: No one may drive a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more (0.08 or more is OWI/PAC).

refusalSuspension.detail: For a first improper refusal, the court revokes the operating privilege for 1 year (occupational license after 30 days) and orders an interlock.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Required at high BAC (0.15%+) or refusal
interlockFirstOffense.detail: First offenders with a BAC of 0.15 or more, or who refused testing, must be ordered to use an interlock and/or a 24/7 sobriety program.

lookback.detail: A second OWI counts priors within 10 years; for a third or later offense, all prior convictions in the person's lifetime count.

name.detail: Driving under the influence of alcohol, controlled substances, or drugs.

bacLimit.detail: Driving in an 'impaired state', which includes an alcohol concentration of eight hundredths of one percent or more, is DUI.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 with a BAC of 0.02% or more (but under 0.08%) commit a misdemeanor and face license suspension.

commercial.detail: Commercial drivers who refuse testing or test at 0.04% or more are disqualified from operating a commercial vehicle.

refusalSuspension.detail: After a criminal-court refusal finding, a first refusal brings a 1-year revocation, or 45 days plus 1 year in the Test and Lock interlock program.

interlockFirstOffense.value: Optional (Test and Lock to shorten revocation)
interlockFirstOffense.detail: First offenders face a 6-month revocation and may join the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock (interlock) Program to drive sooner; it is not mandatory.

lookback.detail: Prior DUI convictions count only if the offense occurred within the 10 years before the current arrest.

name.detail: Driving while under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance.

bacLimit.detail: No person may drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.08% or more, including within two hours after driving.

under21.detail: Drivers under 21 may not drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.02% or more, including within two hours after driving.

commercial.detail: Driving a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04% or more is a CDL-disqualifying offense.

interlockFirstOffense.detail: A first offender with an alcohol concentration of 0.15% or more may drive only interlock-equipped vehicles for 6 months.

lookback.detail: Second and third offense penalties apply to convictions within 10 years of a prior DUI conviction.
